problems.title: Last digit of a power expression
problems.question: Find the last digit of 23³⁹⁵·277−32⁷⁶+3⁷⁷·31.
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and check the result against the question.
formulas: Powers of 3 end 3, 9, 7, 1; powers of 2 end 2, 4, 8, 6.
steps: 395≡3 mod 4 gives last digit 7, so the first product ends 9.
32⁷⁶ ends 6;3⁷⁷·31 ends 3. The final digit is 9−6+3 modulo 10.
problems.note: None of the printed choices is 6.

problems.title: A three-digit palindrome divisible by seven
problems.question: m=aba is a three-digit number and a+b is divisible by 7. What must divide m?
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and check the result against the question.
steps: Every term on the right is divisible by 7.

problems.title: Intersect two sets of multiples
problems.question: How many two-digit positive integers are multiples of both 6 and 8?
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and check the result against the question.
formulas: Their common multiples are multiples of lcm(6, 8)=24.

problems.title: A remainder modulo 45
problems.question: Find the remainder of(5·8·12·17·22)²+325·91 upon division by 45.
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and check the result against the question.
formulas: The product contains a factor 15, so its square is divisible by 225 and hence 45.
steps: The remaining term has remainder(325 mod 45)(91 mod 45)=10·1.

problems.title: A nested custom operation
problems.question: a◇b=(2a+1)/(b−2). Find 5◇(1◇3).
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and check the result against the question.
formulas: Evaluate the inner operation first.

problems.title: A remainder compatible with division by six
problems.question: A leaves remainder 5 upon division by 6. Which listed remainder modulo 24 can it have?
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and check the result against the question.
formulas: A remainder modulo 24 must itself be 5 modulo 6, because 24 is divisible by 6.

problems.title: The fourth digit from the right
problems.question: Find the fourth digit from the right of 24·25·⋯·34.
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and check the result against the question.
formulas: Compute the product modulo 10000;the result keeps exactly its last four digits.
steps: Multiply successively, reducing modulo 10000 each time. The remainders from 24 onward are 24, 600, 5600, 1200, 3600, 4400, 2000, 2000, 4000, 2000, 8000.
The last four digits are 8000, so the thousands digit is 8.

problems.title: A fraction containing mixed numbers
problems.question: Evaluate $\frac{2\frac 58-\frac 23\cdot 2\frac 5{12}}{(3\frac 1{12}+4.375):19\frac 89}$.
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and check the result against the question.
formulas: Convert each mixed number to an exact fraction.

problems.title: Successive deliveries from a storehouse
problems.question: A storehouse sends 1/5 of its oranges to one shop, 1/3 of the remainder to another, and 3/4 of what remains to a third. The third receives 120 kg. Find the original amount.
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and check the result against the question.
formulas: The third receives(4/5)(2/3)(3/4)=2/5 of the original.
steps: If the original amount is M, then(2/5)M=120.

problems.title: A class size from score fractions
problems.question: Fractions 1/6, 1/10, 1/5, 1/3 of a class earn scores 6, 7, 8, 9. The remaining 6 pupils earn 10. Find class size.
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and check the result against the question.
formulas: The four fractions sum(5+3+6+10)/30=4/5.
steps: Thus 6 pupils represent 1/5 of the class.

problems.title: Neither of two languages
problems.question: Of 100 employees, 70 know English, 45 Russian, and 23 both. How many know neither?
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and check the result against the question.
formulas: Inclusion-exclusion:at least one=70+45−23.

problems.title: A set difference that must be empty
problems.question: For nonempty sets A, B, which listed expression is always empty?
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and check the result against the question.
formulas: A⊆A∪B.
steps: No element of A can lie outside A∪B.
Therefore A\(A∪B)=∅, irrespective of how A and B overlap.

problems.title: Reverse a percentage comparison
problems.question: a is 40% of b. What percentage of a is b?
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and check the result against the question.
formulas: a=0.4b implies b/a=1/0.4=2.5.
problems.answer: 250%, assuming the nonzero quantities needed for a percentage ratio.

problems.title: A number one short of three multiples
problems.question: a is the smallest positive integer leaving remainders 2, 4, 6 modulo 3, 5, 7. Find a mod 11.
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and check the result against the question.
formulas: a+1 is divisible by lcm(3, 5, 7)=105.

problems.title: Oil remaining after three deductions
problems.question: Three transit countries retain 20%, 30%, 40% of the oil reaching them. What percentage of the original arrives?
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and check the result against the question.
formulas: Remaining fraction=.8·.7·.6.

problems.title: Two bisectors among four ordered rays
problems.question: Rays OA, OB, OC, OD occur clockwise in that order, and angle AOB+COD=180°. Find the angle between the bisectors of AOC and BOD.
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and check the result against the question.
formulas: Let successive ray gaps be u, v, w, z, with u+w=180°.
steps: The oriented bisector directions are(u+v)/2 and u+(v+w)/2.
Their difference is(u+w)/2=90°. If either angle is taken on its smaller side, the corresponding bisector reverses by 180°, leaving the angle between the bisector lines 90°.

problems.title: Maximum intersections of thirteen lines
problems.question: What is the maximum number of intersection points of 13 lines, with every pair intersecting?
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and check the result against the question.
formulas: Each pair determines at most one point:C(13, 2)=13·12/2.
steps: Choose the lines with no three concurrent to attain all pairwise intersections separately.

problems.title: Maximum regions formed by six lines
problems.question: What is the maximum number of plane regions formed by 6 pairwise intersecting lines?
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and check the result against the question.
formulas: Rₙ=1+n(n+1)/2 when no three lines are concurrent.
steps: The kth added line has k pieces and adds k regions.

problems.title: An angle compared with the other three
problems.question: One angle formed by two crossing lines equals 2/7 of the other three angles’ sum. In the source α<β. Find 3α−2β.
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and check the result against the question.
formulas: If that angle is t, then t=(2/7)(360°−t).
steps: 9t=720°, so t=80°. The other angle size is 100°.

problems.title: Two division points on a segment
problems.question: M divides AB in ratio 4:5 from A;K divides it 5:7 from B. MK=10 cm. Find AB.
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and check the result against the question.
formulas: AM=4 AB/9;AK=7 AB/12.

problems.title: Triangles using points on two parallel lines
problems.question: There are 3 points on one line and 5 on a parallel line. Every point is joined to those on the other line. Count triangles using the 8 marked points as vertices.
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and check the result against the question.
formulas: Choose two vertices on either line and one on the other.
problems.note: This counts triangles whose vertices are the marked points, as the choices intend. Including new intersection points of drawn segments would be a different counting problem.

problems.title: Clock-hand angle at 10:40
problems.question: Find the smaller angle between the hands at 10:40.
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and check the result against the question.
formulas: Minute angle=6m;hour angle=30h+0.5m.

problems.title: Greatest possible distance on one line
problems.question: B, C, D, M are collinear, BC=9, BD=18, DM=5. Find the greatest CM.
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and check the result against the question.
formulas: Triangle inequality along the line gives CM≤CB+BD+DM.
steps: It is attained with B=0, C=−9, D=18, M=23.

problems.title: A parallel-line angle chase
problems.question: In the source AB∥CD and AC∥BD. KCF=48° and BDN=3 MAP. Find PAC.
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and check the result against the question.
formulas: Corresponding and vertical angles give BDN=48°.
steps: Therefore MAP=16°. The angle between ray AM and the upper continuation of AC is 48°.
Measured from the rightward parallel, ray AP has direction 180°−16°=164°, while AC has direction 180°+48°=228°.

problems.title: The best position for a shared well
problems.question: Three houses A, B, C lie in that order on a straight road. One family in each makes one daily well trip. Where should the well be to minimize total travel?
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and check the result against the question.
formulas: The sum of absolute distances to an odd number of equally weighted points is minimized at the median.
steps: Between A and B, moving toward B decreases distances from B, C and increases only the distance from A, so the total falls.
Between B and C, moving away from B increases two distances and decreases one, so the total rises.
